items.title: 52240_Frank _Machito_ Grillo oral history interview
items.q: Mambo U.S.A., which was conceived by George Gomez, to help with your record sales and Tico records sales

ctx.x: As a matter of fact, we heard our records in Japan when we was in 1962, and imagine, that was 1948/'49; and when we went to Japan in 1962, they was playing Continental records up there, numbers that we ......

Okay. Macho, years later on about 1954 - that's almost six years later - Tico Records - George Gomez- ends up with those Continental recordings and they are transferred to Tico. How did that come about?

Well, the Continental, like always, an American company, they haven't got the patience to deal with a Latin artists. First of all because all the records that was singing in Spanish, all the collections that they had with the disk jockeys that it was American, American --- In those days, I don't think we had two stations that was broadcasting Latin music in New York; and in Philadelphia, maybe one; and in Boston, one hour a week or whatever. So it was no chance to publicize, to expose what we record, so they…
